Part 5 Cross-Scale and Cross-Circle Transformations ​

When an object, observation, or action moves from SP0 to SP1, this Part asks what expands, what contracts, which positions are incomparable, what justifies a conversion bridge, and what information the conversion loses. The general process is called scale transformation. The nine axes are compared using a product partial order. The term scale elevation applies only when the relation in that order is strict.

05Note

Understanding this section

Part V: Cross-Scale and Cross-Circle Transformations

Looking farther, aggregating more people, and entering a higher organizational level may expand different things while losing details. Part V first separates “which axis changed,” then asks what establishes the bridge, rather than calling every change an upgrade.

This part denotes the source scale profile SP0 and the target SP1. When discussing changes in objects, observation, or action, specify expansion, contraction, incomparability, conversion bridges, and losses individually. Scale transformation is the general term; scale elevation is a narrower classification, used only when the strict product partial order on the nine axes holds.

The nine axes are aggregation A, space X, time T, organization O, causation C, observational resolution R, influence I, network N, and jurisdiction and authorization J. They are not a single “large-scale score” whose dimensions offset one another. Finer observation does not automatically expand permissions, nor does a higher organizational position prove a more sufficient causal explanation. Complete comparison must also preserve rules, versions, and each axis's semantics.

This part first clarifies contract roles and references, then establishes axis-by-axis comparisons and overall classification. It next distinguishes operator branches and outcome states, explaining the respective bridges, losses, and boundaries of nine operations. Finally it addresses records, protection, independent evidence, cross-circle processes, and recasting. Readers should continually ask whether the current discussion concerns definitions, procedures, mathematical conditions, empirical effects, or eligibility for actual action.

Cross-scale and cross-circle processes are different questions. Scale change concerns variables and representations between SPs; changes in circle relations concern juxtaposition, containment, overlap, or bridging; rewriting sourced expression for another task also involves recasting. These may occur together, but what each preserves, loses, and can fail at must be checked separately rather than collapsed into “successful elevation.”

How the argument develops

  1. 1

    Premise: different uses may change observed objects, scope, resolution, relations, or available actions.

  2. 2

    Decompose the comparison: map source and target onto the nine axes and their semantic fields, seeking reviewable mappings axis by axis without first presuming that the whole is higher.

  3. 3

    Connection to classification: the strict product partial order holds only if every axis is preserved or expanded and at least one expands. Contraction, incomparability, and unknowns are classified separately under later rules.

  4. 4

    Limit on conclusions: classification cannot replace conversion bridges, target evidence, or permissions; assess each loss's effects in relation to the final task.

Distinctions to keep clear

Scale transformation

General change between SPs may be mixed, contractive, incomparable, or unresolved.

≠

Scale elevation

A specific category in which the strict product partial order on the nine axes holds.

Larger scope

May expand only one axis's primary scope.

≠

Stronger overall judgment

Still requires other axes, auxiliary semantics, evidence, and permissions.

Scale change

How variables are preserved or changed between SPs.

≠

Circle relations / recasting

Change relations or expression respectively and cannot share a single closure status.

Teaching construction: aggregating more units while losing detailTeaching scenario

AssumptionsEvery axis relation is an explicitly given teaching condition, not certification of a real statistical system.

Suppose a purely mathematical record changes from a unit-by-unit table to an overall total. Aggregation axis A is established to expand and observational-resolution axis R to contract, while the other seven axes retain the same semantics. Since the nine axes include both expansion and contraction, 5.3 classifies the change as mixed, not scale elevation. Questions about totals may still be answered accurately; questions about tails or specific locations require examining the information lost.

BoundaryThis only demonstrates separation of classification from task evaluation; it does not prove that actual aggregation necessarily uses this mapping.

Teaching construction: knowing only that space expands still does not establish an overall conclusionTeaching scenario

AssumptionsUnknown and expanded are constructed field states; classification follows the explicit order in 5.3.

Suppose expansion of the spatial axis has been witnessed while the other axes remain unchecked. This evidence alone cannot establish overall elevation across all nine axes; retain unknowns and continue comparing. If an axis is later found to be explicitly incomparable, overall classification should prioritize incomparability rather than use ‘some unknowns’ to conceal a known break.

BoundaryDo not write unresolved evidence as actual failure or zero effect.

What counterexamples change

Teaching counterexampleTeaching counterexample: A expands while R contracts, yet the result is called ‘overall scale elevation.’

What it limitsThe strict product partial order requires no contraction on any of the nine axes. Known opposing directions suffice to restrict that label, without preventing usefulness for a particular task.

Historical research manuscript: Xikari: On Conditions, Structure, and Transformation, source text supplied by the user

What does not follow

  • A gain on one axis cannot offset information loss on another and still directly be called elevation. A weighted evaluation requires a separately specified task and values; it does not replace this chapter's partial-order classification.
  • An unknown axis is not an unchanged axis. Nor does J being inapplicable to a purely natural process automatically authorize researchers' actual operations.
  • A larger representation may not better suit the current task; a finer one also has measurement, explanation, and maintenance costs. Directional labels do not imply superiority or inferiority.

Scope and open questions

This unit introduces the part and explains classification scope. Axis-by-axis constructions with explicit assumptions suffice; historical events need not be forced in as evidence for classification rules.

  1. 1

    Why does an aggregate diagram covering more members not necessarily count as scale elevation?

  2. 2

    Does expanding observational scope authorize acting on more objects?

  3. 3

    If a single process involves cross-department communication, data aggregation, and summary rewriting, can one term suffice to assess acceptance?

Why does an aggregate diagram covering more members not necessarily count as scale elevation?

Observational resolution may be lost or other axes' semantics changed at the same time. Overall classification requires comparing all nine axes, not relying on member count alone.

Basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

Does expanding observational scope authorize acting on more objects?

No. The J axis requires independently valid authorization; observational, influence, or organizational scope cannot expand it by proxy.

Basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

If a single process involves cross-department communication, data aggregation, and summary rewriting, can one term suffice to assess acceptance?

They cannot replace individual checks. They may concern circle relations, scale mappings, and recasting respectively; retain each one's inputs, bridges, losses, and results.

Basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

5.1Contract[1] Roles and Unambiguous References ​

In briefThe same letter O can refer to organizational hierarchy or to the claim type for operational procedures. Qualified names and roles prevent referring to the wrong object; they clarify statements but cannot turn a label into real-world evidence.
Codes used in this section (4)
  • U01Candidate Object Interface
  • U11Phase, Transition, and Dissolution
  • M01Aggregation
  • M09Horizontal Transfer

A scale axis is one of nine definitions of kind D with the role scale_axis_definition. The nine conversion operators are procedures of kind O with the role scale_transformation_operator. U01–U11 are definitions of kind D for universal primitives and have the role universal_primitive_definition. Definitions and procedures make no claim to empirical truth. Specific claims of cross-layer causation must link to a pre-registered root-instance. The same requirement applies to object conversion. A null conclusion must also link to such an instance.

Always use qualified IDs for scale entities, from scale_axis:A to scale_axis:J, from scale_operator:M01 to scale_operator:M09, and from universal_primitive:U01 to universal_primitive:U11. The identifier scale_axis:O denotes organizational level. The expression claim_type=O denotes an operational procedure. The only dependencies are inferential_requires, protocol_requires, specializes, and applies_to. Protocols[2] use formal IDs such as CAUSAL, EVIDENCE, ANALOGY, and SOURCE. They must not use Chinese abbreviations or bare axis names.

5.1Note

Understanding this section

5.1 Contract roles and unambiguous references

The same letter O can refer to organizational hierarchy or to the claim type for operational procedures. Qualified names and roles prevent referring to the wrong object; they clarify statements but cannot turn a label into real-world evidence.

This section gives three roles. The nine scale axes are D-type definitions with role scale_axis_definition; the nine transformation operators are O-type procedures with role scale_transformation_operator; U01–U11 are D-type universal-primitive definitions with role universal_primitive_definition. Definitions specify word use, and procedures specify how to operate or evaluate; neither is an empirical truth establishing that a particular real effect has occurred.

Entities are referenced by category-qualified IDs: the nine actual axis IDs such as scale_axis:A and scale_axis:X; scale_operator:M01 through M09; and universal_primitive:U01 through U11. The source's ‘scale_axis:A through scale_axis:J’ names the endpoints of this nine-axis group, not an instruction to generate ten axes alphabetically. The actual set remains SP=〈A,X,T,O,C,R,I,N,J〉.

The most conspicuous repeated name is scale_axis:O versus claim_type=O: the former is the organizational-hierarchy axis, the latter the operational-procedure type. Similarly, R means relations in D0 object fields but observational resolution in SP. Qualified IDs and their contracts prevent confusion. Displays may use plain-language explanations, but actual protocol references retain formal IDs rather than using informal abbreviations or bare axis names as reference keys.

Dependencies strictly distinguish four types, checked against 2.3: inferential_requires is a hard inferential prerequisite indispensable to the conclusion; protocol_requires comprises methodological gates such as evidence, causality, analogy, and source protocols; specializes is domain or subtype specialization; applies_to is the scope of a norm or procedure. Only the first enters the acyclic inference graph. Requiring source checks before publication does not make ‘source checking’ an empirical cause of changes in the object.

Protocols use formal IDs such as CAUSAL, EVIDENCE, ANALOGY, and SOURCE to prevent synonymous abbreviations from referring to the wrong rule. Specific cross-level causation, object transformation, or null conclusions still require linking a preregistered root-instance and checking its evidence and status. Elegant qualified names, correct prefixes, or complete fields do not constitute instance support. For purely descriptive mappings, the corresponding G-specific fields may be marked not applicable under 5.4; do not invent root instances merely to fill references.

How the argument develops

  1. 1

    First determine the current statement's claim_type and role, distinguishing definitions, procedures, and specific empirical claims.

  2. 2

    Locate the entity using a qualified ID, then check whether the actual referent, version, and role match; do not resolve by one letter alone.

  3. 3

    Label each relation as one of the four types. Only hard inferential prerequisites enter the acyclic inference graph; handle the others according to their methodological or applicability responsibilities.

  4. 4

    When a statement contains specific causation, object transformation, or a null conclusion, additionally check the resolvable preregistered instance and its evidence. Clear references are merely a necessary condition of expression, not passage of empirical tests.

Distinctions to keep clear

scale_axis:O

The D-type definitional entity for the organizational-hierarchy axis.

≠

claim_type=O

The claim type for operational procedures; the two cannot substitute as references.

scale_operator:M02

Identifier of the nesting operation procedure.

≠

A particular cross-level causal relation holds

An empirical conclusion for a specific branch and instance; it cannot follow from the identifier.

protocol_requires

A methodological gate required to publish a judgment.

≠

inferential_requires

A hard inferential prerequisite indispensable to the conclusion; only this type enters the acyclic inference graph.

The formal ID resolves

The correct constraint or instance can be located.

≠

The content is true and applicable

Independent evidence and condition checks are still required.

Teaching construction: avoiding incorrect references with the same OTeaching scenario

AssumptionsOnly a constructed reference example; it refers to no real organization or registered instance.

Suppose a comparison record asks whether organizational position changes; it should reference scale_axis:O. Another record specifies use of the nesting procedure; it should carry claim_type=O, role=scale_transformation_operator, and entity scale_operator:M02. Entering ‘organizational-axis expansion’ under claim_type, or treating procedure type O as an organizational node, is a category error. Even with all three fields correct, cross-level causation still requires a separately selected branch and evidence.

BoundaryThis explains the role of types and names, without claiming that a validator has run or that a real mapping has passed.

Teaching construction: a methodological gate must not become an empirical causeTeaching scenario

AssumptionsThe causal sentence is an illustration to be tested, with no real intervention results or fabricated root-instance.

Suppose one plans to publish the causal claim ‘input changes output through a channel.’ The record may list CAUSAL and EVIDENCE as protocol_requires, meaning review under the corresponding methods is required. It cannot record ‘performing the CAUSAL check’ as an additional physical cause of the object's output change. Registering inferential premises, the channel itself, and methodological procedures separately prevents conflating research activities with the process studied.

BoundaryThis does not establish the specified channel or replace experiments or domain research with standardized records.

What counterexamples change

Teaching counterexampleTeaching counterexample: seeing the scale_operator:M02 label and treating descriptive membership containment as cross-level causation.

What it limitsAn operation's name cannot override the evidential responsibilities of different branches; return to the selected mode and real instance.

Historical research manuscript: Xikari: On Conditions, Structure, and Transformation, source text supplied by the user

Teaching counterexampleTeaching counterexample: treating the SOURCE methodological gate as both a hard inferential prerequisite of a conclusion and an empirical cause of object change because ‘publication is impossible without it.’

What it limitsA procedural bar on publication is not a cause of change in the world; register it as protocol_requires.

Historical research manuscript: Xikari: On Conditions, Structure, and Transformation, source text supplied by the user

What does not follow

  • Qualified IDs prevent ambiguity; they do not guarantee that the entity behind a name has occurred, that evidence is genuine, or that authorization is valid.
  • Do not connect everything that ‘needs to be done’ into causal edges, or treat a norm's applicability as evidence that a description is true.
  • When a real process contains multiple operations, later sections should split it into atomic records and connections, rather than hiding their individual failures behind one grand label.
  • This section is not an instruction requiring software to be written or run; machine readability of a specification does not mean domain semantics have been verified.

Scope and open questions

This section formally specifies roles, naming, and dependency types. Constructed records directly expose category errors; historical events need not masquerade as proofs of the specification itself.

Check your understanding

  1. 1

    Are scale_axis:O and claim_type=O interchangeable?

  2. 2

    Why can the nine axes not simply be listed A, B, C, and so on through J?

  3. 3

    If a missing methodological gate prevents publication of a judgment, may it enter the acyclic inference graph?

  4. 4

    Does a correct root-instance ID prefix suffice to support object transformation?

Are scale_axis:O and claim_type=O interchangeable?

No. The former is an organizational-hierarchy-axis entity and the latter a procedure type; the same letter does not mean the same role.

Basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

Why can the nine axes not simply be listed A, B, C, and so on through J?

This book's nine axes are A, X, T, O, C, R, I, N, and J. Naming the endpoints in the source does not specify a continuous alphabetical range; reference the defined set.

Basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

If a missing methodological gate prevents publication of a judgment, may it enter the acyclic inference graph?

Not on that basis. Only inferential_requires hard prerequisites enter; methodological gates still have actual responsibility for constraining publication.

Basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

Does a correct root-instance ID prefix suffice to support object transformation?

No. Resolve the actual registration, version, preselected branch, criterion, and supporting evidence. Neither labels nor hashes replace semantic verification.

Basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

5.2Nine-Axis States and Axis-by-Axis Comparison ​

In brief‘It has grown’ first requires asking in which respect. Member coverage, space, observational fineness, causal models, and authority each have their own comparison method. Drawing a larger diagram cannot answer all nine questions at once.

Each object and transformation is bound to the following:

SP=<A,X,T,O,C,R,I,N,J>

AxisCore State FieldsComputational Witness for expandsLimits on Substitution
A Aggregation LevelUnits, membership set, partition, aggregation rule, weights, and exclusionsThe target population covers the source population, and the target partition is a registered coarsening of the source partitionO, X, I, and J must not substitute for A
X Spatial ExtentCoordinate system, spatial set, boundary channels, and external connectionsOnce the coordinates are aligned, the source space is a proper subset of the target spaceA, O, I, and J must not substitute for X
T Time SpanTime reference, window role, start and end points, and time-lag modelWith the same reference and role, the target interval properly contains the source intervalA current cross-section and a long-term path cannot substitute for each other
O Organizational LevelOrganizational graph, version, nodes, containment edges, interfaces, and overlapsIn the same version of the organizational DAG, the target node covers the ancestor closure of the source nodeA higher position in the organization does not amount to an expansion of J
C Causal LevelCausal model, variables, edges, intervention semantics, and abstraction mappingThe target model covers the source model through a semantics-preserving mapping and adds distinguishable levelsLevel labels, temporal order, and correlation cannot substitute for a causal bridge
R Observation ResolutionMeasurement protocol, distinguishable classes, parameters, error, and protective omissionThe target protocol preserves every distinction in the source protocol and subdivides at least one classHigh resolution does not imply completeness or authority to act
I Scope of InfluenceOutcome, threshold, window, affected positions, and effect orderAfter alignment, the target set of affected positions properly contains the source setNeither influence nor observation amounts to authorization
N Network Topology ScopeGraph and version, nodes, edges, semantics, and sampling boundaryA semantics-preserving graph embedding exists, and the target graph covers the source graphNetwork centrality alone does not identify a center of responsibility
J Scope of Jurisdiction and AuthorizationSet of atomic authorization tuples, each specifying its source, subject, single object, single action, geographic area, validity period, withdrawal, validity, and evidenceThe normalized set of valid target tuples properly contains the source set, and each added tuple has an independent witness to its validityNo other axis can substitute for J. Taking a Cartesian product of the object and action sets is prohibited

An axis can have only five relations: equal, expands, contracts, incomparable, and unknown. A comparison must preserve the source and target states, the rule and version used, the actual mappings or set differences, information loss, and uncertainty. It must allow others to review the comparison. Expansion or contraction must not be registered between identical states. On the same axis, contracts is the inverse of expands. A witness for a nontrivial relation must come from a comparison in the relevant domain. The record cannot supply such a witness by declaring itself “valid.” Without a basis that can be reviewed, the relation remains unknown.

All nine axes must be registered. Whether an axis applies depends on the object. If an entire axis genuinely does not apply, use a not_applicable object with a reason for the axis state and keep the axis in the record. A typical example is a natural process with neither an acting subject nor a concept of authorization. J does not apply to that process, which differs from having an empty set of authorizations. If the axis is inapplicable on both the source and target sides under the same applicability criterion, the witness may mark it equal. If it is inapplicable on one side and applicable on the other, the semantic domain has changed and the relation should be marked incomparable. If the material is insufficient, it remains unknown. This keeps the nine-axis interface stable and avoids imposing the semantics of human institutions on the world broadly conceived.

Comparison on each axis must satisfy reflexivity, antisymmetry, and transitivity. To keep “almost equal” from breaking transitivity, first use equality_rule to normalize axis states into equivalence classes, then define the partial order on the quotient set of those classes. A tolerance may be used only when a pre-registered shared normalizer or fixed binning places both states in the same equivalence class. A rule that directly declares two arbitrary points equal when their “distance is below the threshold” must not be used. Reflexivity requires a normalized state to be equal to itself. Antisymmetry requires that if each of two states is less than or equal to the other, both belong to the same equivalence class. Transitivity holds only when the intermediate state, versions, and witnesses can be composed. Any break in the mappings, coordinates, graph versions, variables, or authorization chain returns the relation to unknown.

The primary quantity compared on an axis does not suffice by itself. If the axis record includes auxiliary states such as boundary channels, time-lag models, interfaces, error models, intervention semantics, or protective omissions, expands also requires composable, semantics-preserving mappings for these fields. If the primary extent increases and the auxiliary semantics conflict with no mapping between them, the relation may only be recorded as incomparable or unknown. This prevents a “wider extent” from passing as a “higher state on the entire axis.”

5.2Note

Understanding this section

5.2 Nine-axis states and axis-by-axis comparison

‘It has grown’ first requires asking in which respect. Member coverage, space, observational fineness, causal models, and authority each have their own comparison method. Drawing a larger diagram cannot answer all nine questions at once.

The scale profile is fixed as SP=〈A,X,T,O,C,R,I,N,J〉. Every object and transformation records all nine axis states. Comparing source and target retains rules, versions, actual mappings or set differences, losses, and uncertainty. The axis explanations below correspond to the original table's three columns: what is compared, what can witness expansion, and what other things cannot substitute.

A, aggregation axis: its state includes units, member set, partition, aggregation rules, weights, and exclusions. An expansion witness must show that the target population covers the source population and the target partition is a registered coarsening of the source partition; identical states do not constitute expansion. More members, changed weights, and exclusion rules cannot be hidden under ‘a larger population.’ Organizational superiority, greater geographic reach, farther influence, or more authority cannot replace this member/partition comparison.

X, spatial axis: specify the coordinate system, spatial set, boundary channels, and external connections. After coordinate alignment, the source space must be a proper subset of the target space to constitute expansion of the principal scope. A longer numerical range need not mean wider physical space; units, origins, and coordinate mappings must be aligned first. More members, organizational hierarchy, or authorization scope cannot replace a spatial-set witness.

T, temporal axis: specify the time reference, window role, start and end points, and lag model. With the same time reference and role, expansion requires the target interval to properly contain the source interval. Observation windows, prediction horizons, intervention periods, and recovery periods cannot be compared merely by counting days. A current cross-section and a long-term trajectory are not interchangeable, and expanding a window does not guarantee preservation of the original lag semantics.

O, organizational axis: specify the organization graph and version, nodes, containment edges, interfaces, and overlaps. The original table requires target nodes to cover the source nodes' ancestor closure within the same version of the organizational DAG, retaining a checkable mapping. Calculate this using the graph's actual containment direction and closure definition. ‘Higher rank’ or greater prominence is not a witness; organizational superiority also does not imply expanded J-axis authorization.

C, causal axis: specify the causal model, variables, edges, intervention semantics, and abstraction mapping. Expansion must cover the source model through a semantics-preserving mapping and add distinguishable levels. Merely adding variable names, drawing levels, or finding temporal order or correlation does not establish a causal bridge. Even with additional nodes, failure to preserve the original intervention meaning prevents directly calling it expansion on this axis.

R, observational-resolution axis: specify the measurement protocol, distinguishable classes, parameters, errors, and protective omissions. To establish expanded resolution, the target protocol must preserve every source-protocol distinction and subdivide at least one class. More digits, more image pixels, or longer files do not automatically satisfy this. Higher resolution is still not omniscience and creates no authority to observe or act.

I, influence axis: specify outcomes, thresholds, windows, affected locations, and effect order. After alignment, expansion requires the target set of affected locations to properly contain the source set. Media coverage, potential contact, and established actual influence are different sets. Wider influence cannot replace J, nor can an overall effect be unconditionally assigned back to every individual.

N, network axis: specify the graph and version, nodes, edges, edge semantics, and sampling boundary. A semantics-preserving graph embedding must exist, with the target covering the source graph. More nodes do not mean old edges and directions are preserved. Network centrality, bridge positions, actually available resources, and centers of responsibility differ; edges missed by sampling must also remain as uncertainty.

J, jurisdiction-and-authorization axis: the state is a normalized set of valid atomic authorization tuples. Each tuple fixes the source, actor, single object, single action, territory, term, withdrawal, validity, and evidence. Expansion requires the target set to properly contain the source set, with an independent validity witness for every added tuple. Lists of objects and actions must not be automatically paired by a Cartesian product; none of the other eight axes can add authority to J.

Only five relations are used for each axis: equal, expands, contracts, incomparable, and unknown. equal means the same axis state under the specified normalization rules; expands means witnessed strict expansion, and contracts is its inverse; incomparable means it is known that the required comparability does not hold; unknown means available grounds are insufficient. Missing evidence cannot be written as known incomparability, and identical states cannot be treated as expansion.

Registering all nine axes does not mean all nine are always applicable. If entirely inapplicable, retain a reasoned not_applicable state instead of deleting the field. For a natural process without an acting agent or a concept of authorization, J's inapplicability differs from applicable authorization semantics with an empty valid-authorization set. If both source and target are inapplicable under the same criterion, the axis witness may be equal; if only one end is inapplicable, the semantic domain changes and the relation is incomparable; if applicability remains unclear, it is unknown. Actual researchers' authority to act does not disappear because J is inapplicable to the natural object.

Each axis's partial order is defined over normalized equivalence classes formed by equality_rule. First classify states using a common normalizer or bins fixed before outcomes, then compare classes. “The distance between two points is less than a number” cannot directly define equality, because such approximate relations need not be transitive. Reflexivity requires a state to be equal to itself; antisymmetry requires states mutually no greater than one another to belong to the same class; transitivity requires compatible intermediate states, versions, and comparison witnesses. If coordinates, graph versions, variables, or authorization chains do not connect, no multistep conclusion may be assembled; retain unknown.

Expansion of the primary range is insufficient. Auxiliary states—boundary channels, delay models, interfaces, error, intervention semantics, and protective omissions—also need composable, semantics-preserving mappings. Known semantic conflicts that cannot connect yield incomparable; missing mappings or comparison material yield unknown. This prevents replacing “the whole axis state is higher” with “the main number increased.”

How the argument develops

  1. 1

    Specify source/target fields on all nine axes, times, versions, and applicability; do not let one axis stand for others.

  2. 2

    Fix equality_rule and comparison rules beforehand, assigning axis states to normalized equivalence classes.

  3. 3

    Use each axis's specific witness to check preservation of its primary range and auxiliary semantics; self-reported validity or simple counts cannot substitute.

  4. 4

    Judge equal, expands, contracts, incomparable, or unknown separately, retaining actual mappings, losses, and evidence locations.

  5. 5

    When combining comparisons, check that the same intermediate state and version are used and witnesses compose; if they break, infer no transitive conclusion.

  6. 6

    Independently review additions of valid atomic authorizations on J; expansions in observation, influence, or organization cannot replace them. Leave overall nine-axis classification to 5.3.

Distinctions to keep clear

A: aggregation coarsening

Combination at the membership and partition levels.

≠

R: resolution refinement

Preserves more distinguishable states, with a different direction and different evidence.

Primary-range expansion

For example, strict containment of sets or intervals.

≠

Axis-state extension

Also requires preservation of auxiliary semantics such as interfaces, error, and delays.

incomparable

Existing material confirms that comparison semantics or the ordering do not hold.

≠

unknown

Insufficient grounds for comparison; do not claim a known break.

J not applicable

Authorization has no meaning for the object.

≠

J as the empty set

Authorization semantics apply, but no valid permission is registered.

Equality under predefined normalization

Identical normalized outputs form genuine equivalence classes.

≠

Pairwise closeness within tolerance

Need not be transitive and cannot directly serve as equality.

Mathematical construction: why approximate closeness is not equalityTeaching scenario

AssumptionsReal numbers, the strict distance threshold, and the floor rule are teaching stipulations; there are no real measurement data.

Take real numbers 0, 0.75, and 1.5, and mistakenly define distance <1 as equality. 0 is close to 0.75, and 0.75 to 1.5, but 0 is not close to 1.5, so transitivity fails. If normalization n(x)=floor(x) is fixed beforehand and equivalence is defined by n(x)=n(y), then 0 and 0.75 belong to class 0 and 1.5 to class 1; equality of equivalence classes is transitive. This binning loses within-class differences, whose acceptability still depends on the task.

BoundaryEstablishes only the logical difference between the relations; it does not claim that this binning is optimal or suitable for every physical quantity.

Mathematical construction: aggregation expansion and resolution contraction can coexistTeaching scenario

AssumptionsFixed population, explicit partition, and summation in common units; source records distinguish each unit, while the target genuinely supplies no components.

The source member set {a,b,c,d} is partitioned into singletons. The target still contains all four members but registers the merged partition {{a,b},{c,d}}. Under an explicit aggregation rule, this can constitute strict coarsening on A; if target observation retains only group totals, differences between a and b may be lost, so R contracts. The two axes point differently; an A witness cannot replace R's, nor justify “all scales increased.”

BoundaryA formal example showing only that the two axes differ; real weights, missingness, and error still require actual material.

Teaching construction: a longer interval with a changed roleTeaching scenario

AssumptionsA time-contract illustration only, with no actual prediction or observation.

Suppose source T records a forecast horizon of the next 0–10 days, while target T records an observation window over the past 0–20 days. Though the second number is larger, the temporal reference, direction, and window role differ; length alone cannot establish expands. A semantic bridge is needed. If the roles are known to be unalignable for this comparison, register incomparable; if material is insufficient, register unknown.

BoundaryDoes not imply that historical observation cannot help prediction; it only limits directly ranking different windows as temporal expansion.

Teaching construction: authorization tuples prohibit automatic cross-pairingTeaching scenario

AssumptionsSimulated files and authorizations are teaching conditions, not real account permissions or legal advice; no file operations occur.

Suppose two valid simulated authorizations permit the same subject to read file A and edit file B, with fixed territory and duration. They are separate tuples and cannot expand into “both files may be read and edited.” Adding “edit A” requires independent validity evidence for that entire tuple; increasing the number of visible files is insufficient.

BoundaryDemonstrates only set and pairing semantics; certifies no real authorization's validity.

What counterexamples change

Teaching counterexampleMathematical counterexample: 0 and 0.75 are close, as are 0.75 and 1.5, but the endpoints are not.

What it limitsA tolerance relation without common normalization is not transitive and cannot serve as equality underlying a partial order.

What it limitsPrimary-range expansion does not establish expands for the whole axis; known conflicts and unknown material must be registered separately.

Teaching counterexampleTeaching counterexample: permission only to read A and edit B is recombined into permission to edit A.

What it limitsSplitting sets and taking their Cartesian product manufactures unauthorized combinations; J prohibits this expansion.

What does not follow

  • The nine axis values cannot automatically be combined into a weighted total; any separately defined task score does not change this chapter's axis-specific partial-order meanings.
  • Equal when both sides are inapplicable means only agreement under the same applicability judgment; it does not confer new capability or permission on that axis.
  • When edge, interface, or causal semantics conflict without a mapping, larger quantities cannot repair the conflict; local witnesses may remain while the overall axis relation is limited.
  • Choosing a normalizer may lose task-relevant distinctions; declare it beforehand and check tolerance. Fixed bins solve the formal transitivity issue, not automatically the truthfulness of measurement.
  • Two comparisons across versions may use the same node name without sharing the same intermediate object; realign them rather than blindly applying transitivity.

Scope and open questions

This section defines nine axes and their comparison witnesses. Mathematical and contractual constructions directly explain partial orders, normalization, and authorization pairing; real events are not used as substitutes for an unestablished complete set of nine-axis witnesses.

  • Real axis-by-axis comparison still requires corresponding domain material, semantics-preserving mappings, and independent grounds for authorization validity; this lesson certifies no actual organization's or account's permissions.

5.3Product Partial Order and Transformation Classification ​

In briefThe nine axes are not an additive score. If one explicitly contracts, another's large expansion cannot offset it; a known incomparability or mixture of increases and decreases cannot be covered over by an unknown elsewhere.

SP0≼SP1 if and only if all nine axes are equal or expands. The strict relation SP0≺SP1 additionally requires at least one axis to be expands. The machine applies the classification rules in this order:

If any axis is incomparable, classify as horizontal_or_incomparable. An unknown relation on another axis does not override known incomparability.

Otherwise, if there is both expansion and contraction, classify as mixed. Two known relations in opposite directions rule out ordering under the product partial order, even if some axes remain unknown.

Otherwise, if any axis is unknown, classify as unresolved.

If all nine axes are equal, classify as all_equal.

If all axes are equal or expands, with at least one expansion, classify as elevation.

If all axes are equal or contracts, with at least one contraction, classify as reduction.

Thus, macro-level aggregation that also compresses resolution is typically mixed and should not be called elevation across the board. Analogies between domains are often horizontal_or_incomparable. With insufficient material, the classification is unresolved. Only instances classified as elevation may be called “scale elevation.” An increase in the scope of observation, space, organization, influence, or network leaves J unchanged. An expansion of J can be witnessed only by new, valid authorization tuples.

If a J state stored “one source + a set of subjects + a set of objects + a set of actions” as independent fields, it would generate object–action combinations that had never been authorized. The authorization_tuple_contract requires each atomic tuple to bind exactly one source, one decision-making subject, one object, and one action and to preserve the geographic area, validity period, withdrawal conditions, evidence, and independent review. Multiple objects or actions must be split into multiple tuples. Only normalized atomic tuples with a valid status enter the set comparison. The witness for J-axis expansion must list, in comparison_payload, the complete tuples added on the target side and absent from the source side, along with independent evidence of their validity. It must align with j_authorization in the record. Arbitrary strings, tuple IDs, self-assertions, actual control, observation coverage, increased influence, a higher position in the organization, and expansions on other axes cannot make J expands.

5.3Note

Understanding this section

5.3 Product partial order and transformation classification

The nine axes are not an additive score. If one explicitly contracts, another's large expansion cannot offset it; a known incomparability or mixture of increases and decreases cannot be covered over by an unknown elsewhere.

The source defines SP0≼SP1 if and only if all nine axis relations are equal or expands; the strict relation SP0≺SP1 additionally requires at least one expands. This is a product partial order: each component must avoid decreasing, and at least one must strictly increase for a strict overall rise. It allows many profiles to remain unrankable and does not try to put all objects on one leaderboard.

Classification order has substantive significance. First, any incomparable axis yields horizontal_or_incomparable: a known comparison break takes priority over unknowns. Second, without incomparability, simultaneous expands and contracts yield mixed; two known opposite directions already rule out the product order even if another axis is unknown. Third, only when neither preceding condition holds and some axis is unknown is the result unresolved.

In the remaining cases all nine axes are compared, without incomparability or opposite directions. All equal gives all_equal; only equal/expands with at least one expansion gives elevation; only equal/contracts with at least one contraction gives reduction. Classification describes transformation direction, not procedural results such as supported/null_supported, and does not judge whether a task improves. Section 5.4 separately handles result-support status.

For example, macroaggregation that compresses component observations may expand A while contracting R, giving mixed. It may help a totals task yet remain outside this definition of elevation. Domain analogies often involve horizontal incomparability, and insufficient material may leave classification unresolved. Do not first name a process “upgrading” and then select favorable axes to justify the name.

J is entirely independent of the other axes. An atomic authorization tuple binds exactly one source, decision-making subject, object, and action, together with territory, duration, withdrawal, evidence, and independent review. Register multiple objects or actions separately; do not split lists and take their Cartesian product to generate all pairings. Only valid, normalized tuples enter set comparison.

J expansion requires the target valid set to strictly contain the source set, with comparison_payload listing complete added tuples and their respective independent validity evidence, aligned with j_authorization. A string, tuple ID, or self-reported “authorized” is insufficient. Observation coverage, actual control, influence range, organizational superiority, and expansion of other axes cannot provide this witness. If new authorization accompanies withdrawal of old authorization, set expansion may not hold; compare anew.

Every classification assumes reliable axis-specific witnesses from the preceding section. A machine can correctly combine wrong inputs, so a correct classification algorithm cannot establish correct domain mappings. If intermediate states, versions, or semantics do not align, two directional comparisons cannot be directly assembled into overall elevation.

How the argument develops

  1. 1

    Mathematical premises: each axis forms a partial order over common normalized equivalence classes, with compatible objects, versions, and semantics across comparisons.

  2. 2

    Explicit derivation of reflexivity: every axis has s_i≼s_i, so the nine-axis product profile satisfies S≼S.

  3. 3

    Explicit derivation of antisymmetry: if S≼T and T≼S, each axis is mutually no greater; antisymmetry on each gives s_i=t_i, so profiles are identical on normalized classes.

  4. 4

    Explicit derivation of transitivity: if S≼T and T≼U with compatible intermediate states and witnesses, axis-level transitivity gives s_i≼u_i and therefore S≼U; a break in version or semantics defeats the premise of this derivation.

  5. 5

    Strict direction: S≺T only if S≼T and at least one axis strictly expands; any known opposite direction or incomparability blocks strict elevation.

  6. 6

    Actual classification: select the first satisfied class in the order incomparable → mixed → unknown → all equal → elevation → reduction; then independently check the complete valid authorization witnesses for J additions.

  7. 7

    Conclusion ceiling: product-order classification is not itself an empirical effect, value ranking, or permission to act; real axis comparisons and authorization validity carry separate evidential responsibilities.

Distinctions to keep clear

mixed

No known incomparability, but known expansion and contraction coexist.

≠

unresolved

Neither preceding known exclusion can yet be established, and some axis is unknown.

horizontal_or_incomparable

At least one axis has an incomparability witness.

≠

unknown

Material is missing; this alone cannot claim known incomparability.

elevation

All nine axes preserve or expand, with at least one expansion.

≠

Greater net benefit

Separately requires task, cost, and distributional evaluation; direction does not imply it.

Transformation classification

How the nine axis relations combine.

≠

Four operator-result states

Whether the selected branch ran, is supported, or meets the zero gate is judged separately in 5.4.

Strict containment of valid tuple sets

Old authorizations remain, with independently valid additions.

≠

More permission fields

May merely mean more text, invalid entries, or unauthorized cross-pairings.

Mathematical construction: three vectors containing unknown yield different resultsTeaching scenario

AssumptionsThese relations are teaching inputs assumed to have corresponding axis witnesses, not actual measurements or authorization records.

Use order (A,X,T,O,C,R,I,N,J). Let A=(expands,equal,equal,equal,equal,contracts,equal,unknown,equal); known expansion and contraction coexist without incomparable, so the class is mixed. For B, change A's I to incomparable: the first-priority class is horizontal_or_incomparable, not overridden by unknown N. Let C=(expands,equal,equal,equal,equal,equal,equal,equal,unknown): there is no known incomparability or contraction, but J is unknown, so it is unresolved, not elevation.

BoundaryIllustrates algorithmic priority, not truth of inputs or whether A is better than B.

Mathematical construction: the final three determinate classesTeaching scenario

AssumptionsAll axes are known and comparable; possible utility here is only a conditional explanation, without real effect measurement.

Nine equal axes give all_equal. Only R expands and the rest are equal gives elevation, provided the R refinement witness and preservation semantics of all other axes actually hold. Only R contracts and the rest are equal gives reduction. Even if contraction makes a task cheaper or protects privacy, its direction remains reduction; desirability separately requires targets and reasons.

BoundaryNeither higher resolution is assumed necessarily beneficial nor lower resolution necessarily wrong.

Teaching construction: complete atomic authorizations and genuine additionsTeaching scenario

AssumptionsAll simulated authorizations are teaching premises; territory, duration, and validity comparisons are aligned, and no real file operation occurs.

Let simulated tuple τ1 bind source Permit1, subject A, object file P, action reading, territory experimental domain, duration days 0–5, withdrawal rule R1, valid status, and evidence E1/independent review V1. τ2 independently binds the same subject to editing file Q. The source set is {τ1,τ2}; only when new τ3 contains every field and independent validity evidence for “edit P” does target {τ1,τ2,τ3} satisfy the set condition for J expansion. Permit1, E1, and similar terms are example labels, not real root instances or actual permissions.

BoundaryDisplaying a set condition is not a review of actual legal or account permissions; actual validity requires genuine independent materials.

Mathematical construction: more entries need not mean expanded authorityTeaching scenario

Assumptionsa, b, c, and d denote normalized complete atomic tuples; the comparison concerns only the valid sets in the corresponding states.

Let the source's valid authorization set be {a,b} and the target's {b,c,d}, where a has been revoked and c and d are new. The target has 3 entries and the source 2, but neither set is a subset of the other. They are therefore incomparable under this partial order of authorization sets; an increased count cannot establish J expansion.

BoundaryThis evaluates neither the normative justification of additions or revocations nor the evidence of each tuple's validity.

What counterexamples change

Teaching counterexampleMathematical counterexample: A expands, R contracts, and N is unknown, but no axis is incomparable.

What it limitsThe result should be mixed, not unresolved, much less elevation; known opposing directions are sufficient to limit the overall ordering.

What does not follow

  • Neither equal-weight nor weighted totals replace the product partial order; a separate score must be explicitly a different question, not a change to this section's definition.
  • Known incomparability takes priority over mixed and unknown, and known mixed directions over unknown; records containing an unknown must not all be classified unresolved.
  • Equality on all nine axes means only equal registered scale states; it does not establish equality of every object state, outcome, meaning, or normative eligibility.
  • Equal when both source and target J are inapplicable creates no permission; an unclear axis comparison must retain its gap. A clear diagram cannot replace substantive grounds.
  • Replacement within an authorization set may yield incomparability even if the number of entries rises; retain validity, source, subject, object, action, territory, and duration.

Scope and open questions

This section formally specifies a product partial order, classification order, and authorization sets. It presents public derivations using complete vectors and set counterexamples, without presenting unregistered real-world events as nine-axis classifications.

Check your understanding

  1. 1

    If one axis is incomparable and another unknown, what is the overall class?

  2. 2

    What if expansion, contraction, and unknown coexist without incomparability?

  3. 3

    If only one axis expands and another is unknown, may this be called elevation?

  4. 4

    If reducing resolution protects privacy, does it cease to be reduction?

  5. 5

    Is adding one authorization ID to J sufficient to establish expansion?

  6. 6

    Can transitivity be applied to two comparisons solely because their axis labels match?

If one axis is incomparable and another unknown, what is the overall class?

horizontal_or_incomparable. Known incomparability takes precedence and cannot be overridden by other unknowns.

Basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

What if expansion, contraction, and unknown coexist without incomparability?

mixed. Two known opposing directions suffice to rule out a product-partial-order relation; unknowns do not alter this known fact.

Basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

If only one axis expands and another is unknown, may this be called elevation?

No; this is unresolved. Elevation requires all nine axes to be equal/expands, with at least one strict expansion.

Basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

If reducing resolution protects privacy, does it cease to be reduction?

The direction may still be reduction. Privacy benefits and task sufficiency are separate evaluations and do not rewrite the partial-order classification.

Basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

Is adding one authorization ID to J sufficient to establish expansion?

Insufficient. Complete valid atomic tuples, independent review evidence, and a target set properly containing the source set are required, consistent with comparison_payload and j_authorization.

Basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

Can transitivity be applied to two comparisons solely because their axis labels match?

No. Intermediate states, versions, coordinates, and semantic witnesses must be composable; matching names do not guarantee the premises hold.

Basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

5.4Operator Outcome Statuses and the Null-Conclusion Check ​

In brief‘Effectiveness has not been established’ and ‘absence of a difference within the specified tolerance has been established’ are different results; ‘not yet evaluated’ and ‘the descriptive mapping has been completed’ are also different results. This section requires each operation to account for its status against its own question selected in advance.
Codes used in this section (2)
  • M01Aggregation
  • M09Horizontal Transfer

The operator_ids of each atomic record must contain exactly one operator. Then selected_operator_branch selects exactly one internal branch from that operator’s branch registry. Finally, claim_mode declares the mode of this evaluation as descriptive_mapping (descriptive mapping), root_hypothesis (an instance of a family of empirical questions), causal (causal bridge), object_conversion (object conversion), or intervention_conversion (intervention conversion). The branch registry specifies which modes each branch allows. The three fields must be compatible and must be frozen before the results are read. Failure at the positive-support check must not lead to a switch of branch or a fallback to a looser descriptive mode. Material from one mode must not be used to rescue another. If an actual process contains multiple operators, it must be broken into an ordered chain of atomic records. The target object and SP1 at each step must align with the source object and SP0 at the next step. Each step must register its own outcome status, evidence, loss, and error. A single overall result cannot close the individual steps.

All operator procedures use the same four outcome statuses:

supported means the bridge, decision rule, and positive threshold for the selected branch all underwent pre-registration and have all been satisfied. A root-instance, a preselected subtype, and a single success criterion are mandatory only for G, causal, object-conversion, and intervention-conversion branches. A purely descriptive branch may mark those G-specific fields not_applicable.

unsupported_or_undecided means bridging is insufficient, or the positive-support check and the null-conclusion check have both failed to pass.

null_supported supports a limited null conclusion only when the pre-registered null_decision_rule and the equivalence or sufficiency test both pass. The rule may require statistical power. It may instead require sensitivity. The applicable requirement and the tolerance must also pass.

not_evaluated means the operator or the relevant branch has yet to run. A branch that has run and established its descriptive bridge can be supported. It must not be downgraded to “not evaluated” merely because it requires no G-instance.

“The result was not statistically significant,” “the outcome appeared unchanged after cutting the link,” “the effect disappeared,” “the simple model performed comparably,” and “the evidence for the target was insufficient” do not by themselves warrant null_supported. This rule applies to every operator from M01 to M09, including the ones concerned with cross-layer causation.

5.4Note

Understanding this section

5.4 Operator-result statuses and the null-conclusion gate

‘Effectiveness has not been established’ and ‘absence of a difference within the specified tolerance has been established’ are different results; ‘not yet evaluated’ and ‘the descriptive mapping has been completed’ are also different results. This section requires each operation to account for its status against its own question selected in advance.

Each atomic record may contain only one operator. Although operator_ids has a plural name, its length must actually be 1; selected_operator_branch then uniquely selects an internal branch from that operator's registry, while claim_mode specifies the evaluation mode. None of the three levels may be omitted: what the operation is called, which branch it takes here, and what type of conclusion it aims to support.

Modes include descriptive_mapping for descriptive mappings, root_hypothesis for empirical question-family instances, causal for causal bridges, object_conversion for object conversion, and intervention_conversion for intervention conversion. The registry specifies which modes each branch permits; all three must be compatible and frozen before results are seen. Freezing supplies a fixed basis for evaluation against the original question, while actual execution, deviations, and consistency with the materials still require checking.

If the positive gate fails, one cannot subsequently change branches or retreat into descriptive mode to rewrite the original test as a success. A new, narrower question may be proposed, but a corresponding new record must be created and the old failure or unresolved result retained; success on the new question does not rescue the old one. Nor may materials from one mode be borrowed to fill the evidence originally missing from another.

supported means the selected branch's bridge, decision rule, and positive threshold were preregistered and actually passed. It always represents bounded support for this question, not certification of the entire object or all uses. G question-family, causal, and object/intervention-conversion branches require a root-instance, preselected subtype, and unique success criterion; these G-specific fields may be marked not applicable for purely descriptive branches. A descriptive bridge that has run and passed the positive gate can likewise be supported.

unsupported_or_undecided means the selected evaluation has begun but bridging is insufficient, or neither the positive gate nor the null-conclusion gate has passed. This may reflect insufficient evidence or include predetermined failure signals; the combined status cannot automatically imply that the corresponding mechanism does not exist in the world, nor may uncertainty be concealed as proven failure.

null_supported means a bounded null conclusion has dedicated support: null_decision_rule must be registered beforehand, and equivalence or sufficiency tests, power or sensitivity requirements, and tolerance requirements must pass. ‘Null’ here can mean no task-relevant difference within the specified target and tolerance, not universal absolute absence. Failure to detect a difference may reflect inadequate sample size, precision, window, or design and cannot replace these gates.

not_evaluated means only that the operator or selected branch has not yet run. It is not a negative result, nor may completed descriptive work be downgraded to unevaluated because pure description does not require a G-instance. Conversely, another branch having run does not establish that this branch has been evaluated.

An actual process can contain multiple operators but must be split into an ordered chain of atomic records: the target object and SP1 of one step align with the source object and SP0 of the next, and each step independently preserves its status, evidence, losses, and errors. Apparent final success cannot overwrite intermediate uncertainty, and failure at one step should not erase other independently established local descriptions. Whether the chain completes the final task requires separate checks of task consistency and composition conditions.

‘Nonsignificant’, ‘apparently unchanged after severing’, ‘the effect disappeared’, ‘the simple model performed comparably’, and ‘insufficient target evidence’ cannot automatically be registered as null_supported. This discipline applies to all M01—M09, including aggregation, nesting, temporal accumulation, institutionalization, emergence, and horizontal transfer; caution is not reserved for obvious causal experiments.

How the argument develops

  1. 1

    Before results, fix a single operator, a unique branch, and a compatible mode; disclose the bridge, positive rule/threshold, null decision rule, and permitted comparison range.

  2. 2

    Check whether the selected evaluation actually ran; if not, record not_evaluated without counting execution of another branch in its place.

  3. 3

    If it ran, judge supported using the prior bridge and positive gate; branches requiring a root instance must resolve the corresponding instance, its preselected subtype, unique criterion, and status.

  4. 4

    When the positive gate fails, independently check the preregistered null decision rule and all three gates—equivalence/sufficiency, power/sensitivity, and tolerance. Register bounded null_supported only if all pass.

  5. 5

    When neither type of support is sufficient, retain unsupported_or_undecided and explain precisely what missing bridges, errors, design inadequacies, or failure signals limit.

  6. 6

    Split multiple operators into a chain and align objects and SP step by step; do not let a final overall status conceal intermediate losses or change the question afterward to rescue the original test.

Distinctions to keep clear

Positive gate not passed

The selected positive claim is not yet supported.

≠

Bounded null conclusion supported

A separately preregistered null rule and three passed gates are required; this is not automatically established as the opposite of the former.

not_evaluated

The selected branch has not yet run.

≠

unsupported_or_undecided

Evaluation occurred, but the corresponding bridge or evidence is insufficient, or the criterion was not met.

Descriptive supported

The selected descriptive bridge actually passed under its rules.

≠

Formal causal or conversion supported

Also requires the corresponding root instance and its additional evidence; these cannot substitute for one another.

Create a new, narrower question

Explicitly change the use while retaining the old result.

≠

Rewrite the old branch after results

This destroys the identity of the original evaluation and may not be used to turn failure into success.

Mathematical construction: not supporting a large difference and supporting a small tolerance are different thingsTeaching scenario

AssumptionsThis is a completely known finite model; exhaustive checking covers all three states and can detect any difference >0.05 exactly. The positive/null rules and tolerances are teaching stipulations, not universal thresholds for real-world statistics.

Suppose a finite state domain contains only a, b, and c, with exact source/target mappings and measurements, and the question fixed before results as the absolute difference in a one-step target. The hypothetical positive rule is maximum difference ≥0.10; the null rule is that every state's difference is ≤0.05. The first complete table is (0,0.02,0.06): its maximum is 0.06, insufficient for the positive gate and also failing the null gate, so it remains unsupported or unresolved. The second table is (0,0.02,0.04): its maximum is 0.04. If exhaustive equivalence checking over the full domain, zero measurement error, and corresponding sensitivity requirements were selected beforehand and all satisfied as planned, this supports the bounded null conclusion that ‘the one-step difference in this finite domain does not exceed 0.05’. Neither table reaches 0.10, but their conclusions differ.

BoundaryThis illustrates gate logic only. An actual operator record must also satisfy the corresponding branch, mode, and required root-instance qualification; this example is not an executed real-world experiment or a formal G instance.

Teaching construction: the descriptive branch ran, while the causal branch has notTeaching scenario

AssumptionsThis illustrates branch statuses without a real institution or observations; the roles of M02 branches follow 5.5.2.

Suppose M02's descriptive_nesting completes its check using the prior membership and boundary mapping and receives descriptive supported, but cross_layer_causal has never been evaluated, so that causal branch is not_evaluated. The former cannot be downgraded to unevaluated because description does not require a G-instance, nor can causation be called supported because both branches belong to M02.

BoundaryNo actual supported instance is manufactured, nor are descriptive facts treated as causal evidence.

Teaching construction: a two-step chain does not share one closing statusTeaching scenario

AssumptionsA purely educational operation-chain plan, with no actual system deployment or fabricated effect sizes.

Suppose step one, M01, completes a descriptive mapping from units to a population and preserves target object P and SP1; step two, M08, is preparing to compress P but has not run. Its source must align with P and SP1, and its status remains not_evaluated. Even if step one is already supported, it supports only its local mapping and cannot mark the entire compression process complete. If step two is later found to discard information needed for the final task, preserve that failure along with step one's existing local support.

BoundaryThis does not claim that support for two operators automatically multiplies, nor does it complete acceptance testing for the joint task.

What counterexamples change

Teaching counterexampleMathematical counterexample: a maximum difference of 0.06 falls short of the positive threshold 0.10 but exceeds the null tolerance 0.05.

What it limitsFailure to pass the positive gate cannot automatically become null_supported; the space between the two gates may remain unresolved.

Historical research manuscript: Xikari: On Conditions, Structure, and Transformation, source text supplied by the user

Teaching counterexampleTeaching counterexample: after the causal branch fails, the causal question is deleted after results and replaced with descriptive supported, while the original study is still claimed successful.

What it limitsRetain the original failure/unresolved result and create a separate record for the new description; do not retrospectively alter the original question to rescue it.

Historical research manuscript: Xikari: On Conditions, Structure, and Transformation, source text supplied by the user

Teaching counterexampleTeaching counterexample: a purely descriptive bridge has passed under predetermined rules but is labeled not_evaluated because G fields do not apply.

What it limitsNot requiring G-specific fields does not mean it never ran; register status according to actual execution and criteria for this branch.

Historical research manuscript: Xikari: On Conditions, Structure, and Transformation, source text supplied by the user

What does not follow

  • The scope of null_supported is constrained by the task, object, window, environment, tolerance, and sensitivity; these qualifications cannot be omitted.
  • Labels such as ‘adequate sample’ or ‘acceptable error’ are insufficient; grounds in design, calculation, or comparison proportionate to the claim in question are required.
  • Keep status and mode separate; a supported pure description produces neither causation, value, nor authorization, and is not inherently below not_evaluated merely because it lacks G fields.
  • An atomic record cannot contain multiple operators and close the case with one success value; every unresolved or failed step in a chain must remain visible in the overall conclusion.
  • Formal constructions can illustrate null-gate logic but do not supply power for real samples or replace required empirical root-instances.

Scope and open questions

This section gives procedural specifications for atomic records, branches, and result statuses. It explains null gates using exact finite models and branch examples, rather than forcibly applying them to historical studies lacking complete preregistration materials.

If cutting a channel appears to make no difference, may ‘no channel effect’ be written?

Not automatically. Check the prior null rule, equivalence/sufficiency testing, power or sensitivity, and tolerance; otherwise it may still reflect inadequate detection.

Basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

A descriptive mapping passed but has no G-instance. Must it be not_evaluated?

No. G-specific fields for a pure description may be marked not applicable with reasons; if the branch ran and its positive bridge passed, it may be supported.

Basis: The source text of this section and the public derivation above

If one process aggregates and then compresses, may operator_ids contain two entries?

Not within one atomic record. Split it into an ordered chain, recording each step's single operator, branch, mode, result, and loss separately.

If the original causal test failed and a descriptive relationship is to be studied separately, how can credibility be preserved?

Create a new record compatible with description, preserve the original causal result, and explicitly identify it as a new question; do not rewrite the old test to make it appear successful.

Why does the first finite-example table, with maximum difference 0.06, receive neither type of support?

It is below the positive threshold 0.10 but above the null tolerance 0.05; ‘not large enough’ and ‘already small enough’ are not the same condition.

After the null gate passes, may ineffectiveness be claimed for every object at every time?

No. It supports only a bounded null conclusion within the predetermined object domain, task, one-step window, and tolerance; extrapolation requires separate evidence.

5.5The Nine Scale Transformation Operators ​

In briefFirst ask ‘what relationship does this step actually change?’, then choose an operator. The nine names are not nine packages for the same aggregation template; each carries distinct responsibilities for materials, bridging, and failure.
Codes used in this section (1)
  • M01Aggregation

Each operator has a distinct semantic_signature. The aggregation statement for M01 must not be copied and passed off as that of another operator.

5.5Note

Understanding this section

5.5 Nine scale-transformation operators

First ask ‘what relationship does this step actually change?’, then choose an operator. The nine names are not nine packages for the same aggregation template; each carries distinct responsibilities for materials, bridging, and failure.

The independent proposition following this parent heading is that operator semantics are not interchangeable. semantic_signature constrains operational identity: M01 aggregates units into a population; M02 embeds members within a boundary; M03 transmits along a temporally ordered path; M04 composes longitudinally across windows; M05 durably writes changes into institutions; M06 generates a target pattern from interactions; M07 represents facts through classification and may separately examine transfer of authorization; M08 compresses representations through a many-to-one mapping; M09 transfers source-domain relations into target-domain candidates.

The same event can involve several operators. For example, meeting minutes first aggregate individual views, then form a lasting rule, which is then implemented by a trustee. These are at least three different questions: whether the aggregation is faithful, whether the rule persists, and whether the implementer received the specified authorization. Passing one question cannot close the others. A composite process must be split into ordered atomic records, each containing only one operator.

‘Growing larger’ does not select an operator. More people may change only the A axis; adding a bridge member may change network paths; compressing something into one sentence may reduce R-axis distinctions; even a larger institution may have no greater J authority. Identify the specific mapping, then compare axis by axis, rather than treating the nine operators as automatic promotion buttons.

The same operator also does not imply the same claim. M02 may merely describe nesting or separately study cross-level causation; M05 may study institutional facts or separately their causal effects; M07’s record of actual acting on behalf does not equal an authority transfer. The branches, modes, and four result states of 5.4 still apply; a familiar operation name cannot replace a predetermined question.

Each of the following nine sections has a distinct bridge, loss, and failure mode. Real material supports only the facts or domain conclusions it covers; mathematical constructions prove only the stated formal relations. Neither gains formal G-instance status merely by appearing in this book’s teaching, and neither creates authorization to act.

How the argument develops

  1. 1

    State source object, target object, and current task step by step instead of choosing a grand name first.

  2. 2

    Use the nine signatures to identify each step’s distinctive transformation; split a multistep process into a chain.

  3. 3

    Choose one branch and a compatible claim_mode per step, fixing success, failure, and null-conclusion rules first.

  4. 4

    For that signature, list relations to preserve, permitted changes, and unrecoverable information.

  5. 5

    Check source domain, target domain, and bridge material separately; do not count the same document under different operators as independent support.

  6. 6

    Preserve states and losses step by step, then separately check the same final task and conditions for joint implementation.

Distinctions to keep clear

Operator identity

What kind of relational transformation this step performs.

≠

Result state

What support the question actually receives; the name itself does not determine the result.

Multiple operators

Different atomic questions within one process.

≠

One universal template

Copying aggregation wording into every operation misses their distinctive bridges.

Scale change

The result of comparing the nine axes under their definitions.

≠

Change of authority

The J axis requires specific valid authorization; it cannot expand automatically with size.

Teaching construction: three steps in a fictional meetingTeaching scenario

AssumptionsPeople, meetings, and acts are constructed; institutional legitimacy and signature validity are not assumed.

Four people submit opinions, and a secretary makes a frequency table (M01). The team writes a decided process into rules for later meetings (M05). Someone else claims to represent the team by signing externally (first classify this as an M07 representation claim or actual acting on behalf). Correct frequencies complete only the first step; sustained effectiveness of rules requires later records, and authorization to sign requires independent valid authorization. Describing all three as ‘aggregating to expand influence’ misses the crucial questions in the last two.

BoundaryFictional records do not certify actual authority; institutional facts and permission to act require separate tests.

What counterexamples change

Teaching counterexampleWriting the bridge for M03 network propagation as ‘adding each unit’s weights’ while omitting path direction, capacity, and arrival times.

What it limitsThis may define a total but does not answer whether a message traveled through the specified channel to its destination; the signature is mismatched.

Historical research manuscript: Xikari: On Conditions, Structure, and Transformation, source text supplied by the user

Teaching counterexampleExplaining M07 representative authority as ‘more represented people means more power’.

What it limitsHeadcount is not an authorization tuple and cannot change J on that basis.

Historical research manuscript: Xikari: On Conditions, Structure, and Transformation, source text supplied by the user

What does not follow

  • The same actual event can have complementary records, but more labels do not increase evidence independence.
  • Pure description can receive bounded support without being forced to promise untested causation or transformation.
  • This classification supplies entry points for questions; it does not establish the existence of any particular historical institution, propagation mechanism, or new entity.

Scope and open questions

The parent unit specifies the semantics of operation types and uses explicit constructions to identify questions; empirical mechanism cases are not forced onto it.

  2. 2
